titolo: Trump Calls Putin 'Friend' — Then Can't Speak For America
angolo: Day 6: Trump's 'I can't speak to America' answer, Zelensky's 'Yalta 2 failed' claim after 111 missiles, and Putin's invitation sending Europe to Moscow.
descrizione: Trump Calls Putin 'Friend' — Then Can't Speak For America. On Friday Trump defended calling Putin a friend but said he 'can't speak to America' on whether Putin is a friend of the US. On Saturday Zelensky said the Shenzhen summit was 'very unsuccessful' for Putin, hours after a 111-missile barrage. Meanwhile Putin has invited Europeans to Moscow, and Bloomberg reports the E3 are weighing it. Every fact here comes from AP, CNN, Bloomberg, the Jerusalem Post and other cited outlets.

scene.testo: A hundred and eleven missiles in one night, according to Zelensky. Ukraine's sky lit up.
Hours after Trump, Putin and Xi met together in China.
Now Donald Trump is being asked: is Putin a friend to America?
His answer has drawn wide attention. He said: I can't speak to America.
The big question: what does Trump's friendship with Putin actually deliver?

grafica.sotto: Trump, Putin and the Shenzhen fallout

scene.testo: First, the scene. Shenzhen, Thursday, November 19. A first-ever three-way summit of Trump, Xi and Putin.
Trump, Putin and Xi sat down together for the first time.
Trump greeted Putin warmly and repeatedly called him his friend, AP reports.
Friday, back at the White House, he was asked about it directly.
AP reports he made no effort to walk the comments back.
He did say Putin would love to end the war.
But whether Putin is a friend to America? Trump said he can't speak to that.
CNN's Kaitlan Collins asked the question. Trump moved straight to his own relationship with Putin.
He called it a very good relationship, and said it helps keep the US safe.
But a sharper response was still coming. It came from Kyiv.
Zelensky told CNN it's up to Trump how he describes Putin.
But for Ukraine, he said, the picture is different.

citazione.testo: For us, he is an enemy… for us he's a killer

scene.testo: Zelensky also argued that calling Putin a friend sends a signal.
In his words, Putin then 'doesn't feel enough pressure'.

visivo.testo: In his words, Putin then 'doesn't feel enough pressure'.

scene.testo: Trump's own framing was different. He pointed to hatred between two men.
He said Zelensky and Putin hate each other, and both are stuck in the war.

citazione.testo: You have two people that hate each other, Zelenskyy and Putin.

scene.testo: The war is now more than four years old.
And then came Saturday. Zelensky made a second, bolder claim.
The summit, he said, was very unsuccessful for Russia.

citazione.testo: The summit was very unsuccessful for Russia.

scene.testo: Why? Zelensky says Putin wanted a new Yalta, a redrawing of the world and its borders.
Yalta, 1945. The conference where the US, Britain and the USSR agreed on the post-war order in Europe.
Zelensky said Putin's 'Yalta-2' did not work out.
He noted China refused to be drawn into such an arrangement.
And no public agreements on Ukraine or borders came out of Shenzhen.
That is Zelensky's reading. We found no Kremlin endorsement of it.
But there's a detail that adds weight: a deleted paragraph, according to Finland's president.
Finland's president Alexander Stubb says the draft declaration had a Ukraine paragraph.
He says the United States asked for it to be removed.
Stubb did not say what the paragraph contained. He said the wording was poor.
He said removing it was a good thing.
Stubb explained that the draft contained no call to stop supporting Ukraine, according to European Pravda.
The final text, titled 'Declaration towards Peace', makes no mention of Ukraine.

visivo.testo: The final text, titled 'Declaration towards Peace', makes no mention of Ukraine.

scene.testo: The declaration also called on the ICC to exercise restraint in pursuing state leaders.
Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant issued in March 2023 over the unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children.
Stubb also described a phone call. He said Trump called in to the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin from his plane.
According to Stubb, Trump said the war in Ukraine should end so that Europe can spend its money on other things.
But then another twist. Putin invited the Europeans to Moscow.
Putin said Russia had invited the Europeans to come to Moscow.
Putin said Europeans must travel there if they want a seat in talks.
Putin said that after hearing Europe's position, Russia would decide the format for further talks.
Bloomberg also reports, citing sources, that the E3 – France, Germany and Britain – are weighing a meeting with Russia.
Bloomberg's sources say a national security adviser from one of them spoke with Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov.
Ushakov proposed Moscow as the venue, according to Bloomberg's sources.
No meeting has been confirmed as agreed.
Germany's defense minister Boris Pistorius says: talks, yes. Moscow, no.
He says rejecting the invitation outright would send the wrong signal.
Talks, he says, should happen only if there is a ceasefire.
Zelensky says European leaders will not go to Moscow, though his comment referred to national security advisers.
Finland's Stubb has a different view. He thinks European leaders will have to meet Putin at some point.
Asked about Moscow, Stubb said it was difficult to say at this point.
Stubb also says Trump hinted the Europeans should talk to Putin directly.
So Trump reportedly nudges Europe toward talks with Putin. Zelensky says European leaders won't go to Moscow.
And behind all of it, the FT reports a ticking clock.
Per the FT, Trump's administration wants a Ukraine deal by early January, before Democrats take control of Congress.
According to the Financial Times, Democrats are expected to push stronger support for Kyiv.
They are also expected to push more pressure on Moscow.
Zelensky says NATO membership is still the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine.
Trump touted the summit, while CNN describes it as historic but generating little substantive progress.
So who is right? The facts are mixed.
Confirmed by AP: Trump defended calling Putin a friend, and said he can't speak to America.
Zelensky said the summit was very unsuccessful for Russia, and cited a 111-missile barrage.
Reported only: the E3 weighing Moscow, per Bloomberg's sources, and the deleted paragraph, per Stubb.
What to watch next: whether any European envoy travels to Moscow.
And whether Trump's January deadline forces a deal Kyiv can accept.
